Import from Amazon S3, Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, Snowflake, and Databricks.
Transform with built-in steps (handle missing values, encode categories, scale numbers, featurize text and dates) or your own Python, combined into a data flow.
Data Insights and Quality Report: finds missing values, outliers, duplicates, target leakage, and class imbalance before you train.
Export the flow to S3, a SageMaker Pipelines step, Feature Store, or a Python script, so the same preparation runs in production.

Missing values: drop rows or columns, or impute with the mean, median, most frequent value, or a model. Outliers: detect (for example with Random Cut Forest or z-scores) and cap, transform, or remove. Duplicates: remove, especially across training and test sets (task 1.3.7).

Class imbalance (task 1.3.5): oversample the minority class (including synthetic examples with SMOTE), undersample the majority class, use class weights, augment images or text, and judge the model with precision, recall, F1, or AUC instead of accuracy.

Splits: separate training, validation, and test data; shuffle before splitting unless the data is a time series, which must be split by time; use stratified splits so each set keeps the class proportions; use cross-validation for small datasets (task 1.3.3).

Formats (task 1.1.5): ParquetApache ParquetAn open-source columnar file format for analytics that stores compressed columns along with the schema. Querying Parquet files with Amazon Athena scans less data than CSV or JSON, so it is faster and cheaper.Glossary entryClose or ORC for columnarColumnar storageStoring data column by column instead of row by row, so that analytical queries read only the columns they need, and similar values compress well. Amazon Redshift and the Parquet and ORC file formats store data this way.Glossary entryClose analytics and large training sets, CSV or JSONJSON (JavaScript Object Notation)A text format for structured data made of name-and-value pairs and lists, such as {"bucket": "logs"}. IAM policies, most AWS API responses, and many CloudFormation templates are written in JSON.Glossary entryClose Lines for simple exchange, RecordIO-protobuf for some built-in algorithms.
Same values in training and inference→ leads to Feature Store (online plus offline)
Lowest-latency feature lookups→ leads to InMemory online store
Feature values as of a past date→ leads to Offline store in S3
Humans label images, sensitive data→ leads to Ground Truth, private workforce
Cut labeling cost→ leads to Automated data labeling
One group underrepresented→ leads to Clarify pre-training bias
Visual transforms, export to a pipeline→ leads to Data Wrangler in Canvas
Repeatable Spark or scikit-learn step→ leads to Processing job
Rare positive class→ leads to Oversample, SMOTE, class weights
Skewed numeric feature→ leads to Log transformation
Data Wrangler is now in SageMaker Canvas: import, transform, check quality and leakage, and export to Pipelines or Feature Store.
Feature Store's online store serves the latest values at low latency; the offline store in S3 keeps history for training, and syncing them avoids training-serving skew.
Ground Truth labels with human workforces, and automated data labeling cuts the cost.
Clarify measures bias before and after training and explains predictions.
Know the feature engineering techniques, how to handle class imbalance, and how to split data without leakage.

This deep dive covers the SageMaker AI features for preparing data and features for training, at the depth of the MLA-C02 exam (Domain 1, which is 28% of the exam). It also covers the feature engineering and bias techniques that the exam asks about whatever the tool. For the service as a whole, start with the Amazon SageMaker AI tutorial.

Data preparation on AWS often starts outside SageMaker AI: AWS Glue and Amazon EMR transform data at scale, AWS Glue DataBrew cleans it visually, and AWS Glue Data Quality checks rules. SageMaker AI adds the steps closest to the model: exploring and transforming data for MLML (Machine learning)Software that learns patterns from example data to make predictions or decisions, instead of following rules written by hand. A model is first trained on data, then used to make predictions on new data, which is called inference.Glossary entryClose, storing features for training and serving, labeling, and measuring bias.
Data Wrangler prepares data for ML with little or no code, and is now part of SageMaker Canvas, where you can also describe transformations in natural language.

A SageMaker Processing job runs a script (scikit-learn, Spark, or your own container) on managed instances for pre-processing, feature engineering, and evaluation, reading from and writing to S3. Choose it to run the same transformation code repeatedly in a pipeline, without keeping a cluster up.

Amazon SageMaker Feature Store stores features so that the same values are used to train and to serve, which avoids training-serving skew. Features live in feature groups, each record identified by a record ID and an event time.

With both stores on, Feature Store keeps them in sync. Ingest features in batches (for example from a Processing job, Glue, or EMR) or as streams with PutRecord, for example from a Lambda function or Apache Flink reading Kinesis (tasks 1.1.9 and 1.2.2). Applications in a VPC reach the Feature Store Runtime APIAPI (Application programming interface)A defined way for one program to ask another for data or actions, such as a set of HTTPS requests and responses. Every AWS service is controlled through its API, which the console, the CLI, and the SDKs call for you.Glossary entryClose privately through an interface VPC endpointVPC endpointA private connection from a VPC to an AWS service or another endpoint service without crossing the internet. Gateway endpoints, for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB, are route table targets; interface endpoints are network interfaces that use AWS PrivateLink.Glossary entryClose.

Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth labels data for training with human workers: images (classification, bounding boxes, segmentation), text, video, and 3D point clouds. Choose a private workforce (your employees) for sensitive data, a vendor workforce, or Amazon Mechanical Turk for public data. Automated data labeling trains a model on human labels and labels the confident cases automatically, sending only uncertain ones to people, which lowers cost. Ground Truth Plus provides an expert workforce and project management as a managed service (task 1.3.2).

SageMaker Clarify measures pre-training bias in the data before you train, for a facet such as age or gender: for example class imbalance (one group has far fewer examples) and the difference in proportions of labels (one group gets positive labels more often). After training, it measures post-training bias in predictions and explains them with feature attributions (SHAP). Clarify runs as a Processing job and its reports appear in SageMaker Studio (tasks 1.3.3 and 1.3.4).

Tree-based models such as XGBoost don't need scaling; linear models and neural networks do. Fit scalers and encoders on the training data only, then apply them to validation and test data, to avoid leakage.

Processing jobs, Data Wrangler, and labeling jobs use IAM execution roles; encrypt data and outputs with KMS keys; run jobs in your VPC with S3 endpoints; use a private Ground Truth workforce for sensitive data. Remove or mask personal data before training (task 1.2.8), for example with Amazon Comprehend PIIPII (Personally identifiable information)Information that can identify a person, alone or combined with other data, such as a name, email address, or passport number. Amazon Macie finds PII in Amazon S3.Glossary entryClose detection or Amazon Macie for data in S3.
The offline store keeps a durable history in S3, so training sets can be rebuilt; pipelines rerun failed Processing steps.
Use Spark (Processing jobs, EMR, or Glue) for large datasets, columnar formats, and the InMemory online store for the lowest serving latency.
Pay for Processing and Canvas instance time, Feature Store reads, writes, and storage, and labeling per object. Automated data labeling and a smaller human-labeled sample lower labeling cost.
Processing and labeling jobs write to CloudWatch Logs and report state changes to EventBridge; CloudTrail records the API calls.
